Windows that stay where they're put (menu tabs, friends & chats, a friend's own chat), the public squares kept open by the relay's own host, villages hosted by the server rather than a player, a console to look after them, and a relay of one's own choosing.

**Pinned windows**
- **▣ pin** in the menu's title pins the tab showing (Village, Sound, Online…) as a window of its own over the village. Its settings work there as in the menu. Its title bar moves it, **_** folds it to its title bar, **✕** unpins it, and it's kept where it was put through restarts.
- **Friends & chats** moves by its title bar too. **▣ pin** keeps it open where it's put, and **_** folds it to its title bar. Esc folds a pinned one rather than putting it away, and **✕** unpins it.
- **A friend's own chat, pinned**: *▣ pin Sam's chat over the village* in a friend's **⋯** puts a small window of their own over the village. It shows their latest lines (read as they come), what's new while it's folded, and a line to write the next. It moves, folds and closes the same way.
- Up to 12 pinned in all, the same on the desktop, the web page and the phone.

**The public squares, kept open**
- The relay now has its own host beside it (`xmas-tui --host`, a container): it keeps the four squares open all the time, so the townsfolk, animals and their names are the same for everyone, whoever comes and goes. Without it, a square is hosted by its first player, as before.
- **Server villages**: villages the relay's host keeps open, rather than a player's game. Some are listed in Public villages (marked *· server*). Private ones are reached only with their code.
- **The public list** comes in the relay's order: featured ones first (★), then the rest, busiest first.

**Looked after**
In the villages the relay's host keeps, the relay's keeper can, from its console:
- see who's there and what's been said aloud lately;
- quieten someone (what they say isn't passed on);
- send someone home;
- keep a village or a player out of the relay;
- greet newcomers, and make announcements now or at set times, which show in the post with a chime.

Only the relay's own host can speak for the relay. It signs in with a secret, and what anyone else sends on its topics is dropped. A ban on a player holds when they come back, by a player tag worked out one way from their friend code.

**Another relay**
- Menu → Online → **Relay** takes another relay's address: one run by a club, a school or a group of friends. It then comes first, and its squares' settings, public list and announcements are believed as its own. *Use the village's own* goes back.
- Running one takes the two containers in `relay/`. [SELF-HOSTING.md](https://github.com/dash1101/xmas-tui/blob/main/relay/SELF-HOSTING.md) covers it.

**Privacy**
[PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/dash1101/xmas-tui/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) now covers:
- the player tag;
- what the relay's host sees in its villages, and what it sends the console (who's there, and the last 60 lines said aloud in each, in memory only, gone two minutes after it stops sending them);
- bans, mutes and server villages, and how long each is kept;
- another relay being its operator's own responsibility.

**Relay 1.3.0** (`ghcr.io/dash1101/xmas-relay:1.3.0`, with `ghcr.io/dash1101/xmas-host:1.25.0` beside it): the host's sign-in (`HOST_TOKEN`), bans of villages and players, server villages, the public list's order, featured places and extra starred-out words, mutes, welcomes and scheduled announcements, and the console pages for all of it. Addresses on a private network or the machine itself are no longer counted against the per-address connection limit, so the host and anything else run alongside can't be locked out by it. For a relay behind a proxy of its own rather than Cloudflare, `IP_HEADER` names the header the proxy puts the player's address in (believed only from the proxy beside it), so the limit and blocked addresses work there too. The host says in its log when it's signed in, and when the relay turns it away (a wrong `HOST_TOKEN`). [DEPLOY.md](https://github.com/dash1101/xmas-tui/blob/main/relay/DEPLOY.md) has the steps.
